raw.etymology_text:
From Middle High German mugen, from Old High German mugan, from Proto-West Germanic *magan, from Proto-Germanic *maganą, from Proto-Indo-European *megʰ-.
Compare Dutch mogen, English may, Icelandic mega, Gothic 𐌼𐌰𐌲𐌰𐌽 (magan), Serbo-Croatian moći, Bulgarian мога (moga).
The modern sense of "like" developed out of a negated "nicht mögen", shifting from "to not be able to do" to "to not like doing" in the 16th century, with the original sense "be able to" falling out of use in the 17th century.
See können for the origin of the historically unexpected umlaut.
